question: Can the round-04 equality correction and the round-03/04 stoplist discrepancy be audited from retained artifacts? This is evidence collection only: do not rerun the benchmark or choose a new comparison after seeing a result.
intended_receiver: Authorized local AEG/Surface operator via Mingli
fixed_question_reference: request-04.json: source/rule bindings plus frequency, rank, occurrence locator and selected short excerpt; contextual meaning is outside equality

requested_evidence.request: Provide authorized retained code for result construction, original full-object comparison, corrected declared-field comparison, and index source/rule validation. Identify relevant code versions/digests and dependencies. Include B/R timer start/stop locations or their retained code references so asymmetric process boundaries can be inspected without another benchmark. Do not present an incomplete excerpt as the whole executed program.

Provide the retained full baseline and reloaded objects used by the FIRST comparison, its false result/log if retained, and the exact corrected projection. Keep the extra content_tokens field visible. Bind all to source/rule/index versions if the original record does. Distinguish original recorded output from a reconstruction made now; a reconstruction is not the missing original failure evidence. Do not edit prior receipts.

Provide the ACTUAL round-03 and round-04 stoplist representations from retained code/artifacts, their hash scope/encoding and set differences (added/removed words). A set-size or token-total difference alone does not identify changed words. If the round-03 inline code was not retained, say NotAvailable; do not infer a convenient old stoplist from the observed counts. Also state whether text-layer versions or other rules changed.

known_receiving_side_check: The displayed round-04 stoplist has 119 distinct words. Sorting these words lexicographically and joining with newline with no trailing newline reproduces the declared stoplist SHA-256. This encoding was inferred by the receiver; please confirm the actual producer encoding or correct the interpretation. Full source, rule-module and index hashes remain unverified without their bytes.

requested_projection.task: Name which retained artifacts were located and their original source/rule/record versions.
requested_projection.result: Report original-vs-reconstructed availability, the exact comparison correction and known stoplist additions/removals. State code/attachment references and whether hash encoding was confirmed.
requested_projection.residual: List missing originals, redactions, dependencies or unavailable versions. No new performance conclusion; distinguish inspected evidence from inferred explanations.

optional_attachments.per_artifact: filename or opaque reference, SHA-256 when known, original origin event/version, current disclosure event, and provenance status OriginalCopy / ExtractedFromRetainedArtifact / ReconstructedNow / NotAvailable; list redacted fields and reason
optional_attachments.validation_boundary: Artifacts are data for review. The ordinary checker validates only the response projection; incoming code is not executed automatically. Missing/redacted comparison fields prevent claims about full-object equality. Hashes do not authenticate historical execution.

permission_boundary: Only authorized code and records. No private paths, secrets, full documents or unbounded logs. Bound excerpts/objects; if original objects exceed the disclosure limit, describe the omitted fields and retain completeness as Unknown. Do not strip an inconvenient field and label the remainder a complete original object.
budget_enforcement: The responding operator enforces one 30-second artifact-inspection attempt. At the limit, return partial evidence with missing items. No fresh B/F/R trials, no source recrawling, no index regeneration and no reconstruction disguised as an original. The receiver cannot remotely enforce the sender budget.
acceptance_scope: Auditability of one finite equality correction and rule-history difference. No automatic semantic acceptance, source faithfulness, native identity/free, acceleration or universal grammar claim.
